title: RL Post-training
description: Training progress, rollout timing and Megatron updates for sync and async runs. Select the training type, run, job and executions to inspect. Panels labelled run-wide cover the whole run. Missing telemetry is unknown.

params.value: SELECT run_id AS value FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND name IN ('lifecycle', 'policy_step', 'rollout_call') AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND run_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY run_id HAVING (CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN json_get(resource_attributes_json, 'training_type') = 'async' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 'async' ELSE 'sync' END) = ${training_type:sqlstring} ORDER BY MAX(timestamp_ms) DESC

SELECT job_id AS value FROM (SELECT * FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring})) GROUP BY job_id HAVING job_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY MAX(timestamp_ms) DESC

SELECT execution_uid AS value FROM (SELECT * FROM "telemetry_v1.marinskyrl" WHERE service = 'marinskyrl' AND timestamp_ms >= CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{from}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND timestamp_ms < CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM {{to}}) * 1000 AS BIGINT) AND COALESCE(NULLIF("cluster", ''), 'marin') IN (${cluster:sqlstring}) AND run_id IN (${run:sqlstring}) AND job_id IN (${job:sqlstring})) GROUP BY execution_uid HAVING execution_uid IS NOT NULL ORDER BY MAX(timestamp_ms) DESC

panels.title: Current step
panels.description: Most recently observed completed optimizer step in the selected attempts. A flat value can mean progress stopped; compare the step and record ages. The newest reporting execution wins after a restart, even if its step number is lower.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Steps / hour
panels.description: Observed step progress per hour for the latest step-reporting execution in the selected window. A falling rate means updates are slowing. The rate needs two different observation times and includes pauses between them; it is not a target or projection.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Latest raw reward
panels.description: Latest raw training reward in the selected attempts. Compare its trend and evaluation scores before judging learning. The latest observation wins regardless of reward magnitude; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Generated tokens / s
panels.description: Generated response tokens per second in the latest observed completion bucket. Falling throughput with an empty buffer suggests generation pressure. Completions can be bursty and the latest bucket can be partial; this is not live engine utilization.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Since last step
panels.description: Age of the latest completed optimizer step relative to the selected window end. Green is under 300 seconds, orange is 300–899 and red is at least 900. Compare record age: fresh records with an old step can indicate a stalled trainer.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Since last record
panels.description: Age of the latest selected policy, training-metric or lifecycle/export record relative to the window end. Old steps with fresh records suggest a trainer stall; both ages rising suggests missing telemetry. Green is under 300 seconds, orange is 300–899 and red is at least 900.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Services reporting (run-wide)
panels.description: Distinct services reporting this run in the selected clusters and window. A lower count can explain blank panels; inspect the service table in Diagnostics to see which exporter is absent. Run-wide: Job and Execution do not filter this count.

defaults.noValue: No services reporting this run.

panels.title: Staleness p95
panels.description: Latest per-execution p95 policy staleness among admitted groups. Zero means current-policy data; rising values approach the configured staleness allowance. Sync runs show zero, and absent observations remain empty; rejected groups are excluded.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations in this window.

panels.title: Training reward and informative groups
panels.description: Raw training reward, reward/avg_pass_at_{n} and the fraction of informative groups. Compare sustained reward changes with held-out evaluation; an uninformative group fraction near one leaves little relative training signal. Reward scales depend on the task, and pass-at-n depends on group size; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Evaluation scores
panels.description: Held-out evaluation scores by metric and execution. Use repeated evaluations to check whether training reward improvements generalize. Evaluations are sparse and task scales differ; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Evaluation response length and stop coverage
panels.description: Mean/maximum evaluation response length and stop-class fractions. Rising length limits can explain score changes caused by truncation; compare fractions only at complete stop-reason coverage. Evaluations are sparse and incomplete fractions stay blank; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No supplemental evaluation observations

panels.title: Evaluation score contributions by stop class
panels.description: Evaluation score contributions from length-stopped and completed responses, alongside the overall score. Use them to identify which stop class drives a score change. Contributions need not sum to the overall score because coverage and aggregation differ; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No supplemental evaluation observations

panels.title: Length stops and coverage in trained groups
panels.description: Fraction of consumed responses stopped by a length limit, alongside stop-reason coverage. A rising fraction can mean truncation is discarding useful response tails. The fraction is blank unless coverage is complete; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Optimizer loss and KL
panels.description: Policy loss, final loss and policy KL by optimizer step. Sudden changes can reveal an unstable update; compare KL with the configured target and loss with its recent range. Signs and scales depend on the objective, so these series are not additive; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Gradient norm and policy entropy
panels.description: Gradient norm and policy entropy by optimizer step. Sudden norm spikes can precede unstable updates; collapsing entropy can indicate reduced policy diversity. These quantities have different scales and separate axes; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Optimizer step, synced and producing policy
panels.description: Completed optimizer steps, synchronized model versions and the policy version producing new work. A widening gap means generation is using older weights; a flat optimizer line means progress stopped. Series stay separate by execution; synced versions require trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No policy_step rows in this window. Check the selected Job and Execution, then Services reporting.

panels.title: Generated and consumed response tokens / s
panels.description: Generated response tokens and consumed response/loss tokens per second. Sustained generation below consumption drains the buffer; generation above consumption fills it. Rates use display buckets and completions, so short bursts need a longer window; consumed-token series require trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Rollouts and samples completed
panels.description: Completed trajectories and generated response segments per display bucket. Falling completions can explain a draining training buffer; compare samples with rollouts to spot changes in trajectory structure. These are completion-counter deltas, not in-flight work.

panels.title: Where does the step’s wall clock go?
Rollout wait vs train step (critical path)
panels.description: Mean rollout-wait and optimizer-step wall time, separated by outcome. Rollout wait above training wall suggests generation is limiting progress. Failed spans record only time before failure, and these inclusive walls must not be added. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

panels.title: GPU utilization on this run's nodes
panels.description: Mean busy percentage across the GPUs on nodes attributed to this run. Long steps with low busy percentage suggest devices are waiting; compare with driver wall and generation waits. Node attribution credits each bucket to the run with the most observations, so shared nodes are not partitioned by GPU or rank; requires node-agent reporting. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers. GPU detail is available for ranges of 7h or less; longer ranges show a zoom message.

defaults.noValue: No GPU data. Over 7h: zoom to 7h or less. Otherwise no node join: trainer rows carry no node_name, or the node agent is not reporting this cluster. This is never “GPUs idle”.

panels.title: Step composition: exclusive seconds per span
panels.description: Mean exclusive wall seconds per full driver step and span, separated by execution. Growing components identify where a step spends more wall time; signed negative residuals reveal overlapping observations. Execution series are not stacked, and core-normalized fractions below use a different denominator. Requires inclusive-wall step spans from telemetry export.

defaults.noValue: No inclusive-wall driver rows under root='step'. This build publishes no step timings.

panels.title: Driver step, preparation and policy walls
panels.description: Mean driver step and nested preparation/training walls. Compare changes in the outer step with its child spans to locate a growing wait; nested walls are not additive. Elapsed wall time includes waits and asynchronous device launches; telemetry export enables these spans.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Weight sync and policy offload walls
panels.description: Weight synchronization and related policy walls by outcome and execution. Growth here reduces time available for useful training or generation. Optimizer offload is included in sync_weights, and synchronization-state initialization is startup-only; these are elapsed waits, not GPU kernel timings.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Weight-sync stages
panels.description: Training and weight-sync intervals with completion markers for synchronized weights. Longer or irregular sync intervals identify distribution delays between useful updates. Intervals require trainer.rollout_spans and completion markers require trainer.training_metrics.

panels.title: Core and cycle duration
panels.description: Core training-loop wall and full cycle wall, including time outside the core. A growing cycle/core gap points to evaluation, checkpoint or callback work. The core includes buffer wait, training and weight sync; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Core wall fractions
panels.description: Buffer-wait, training and weight-sync shares of the async core wall. A large wait share suggests generation starvation; rising sync share identifies weight-distribution cost. These core-normalized fractions differ from the full-step exclusive seconds above; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Generation worker await duration
panels.description: Mean and maximum generation-worker waits for prompts, admission slots, queues, model calls and environments. Rising model waits suggest serving pressure; slot waits with a full buffer can be expected backpressure. The mean divides wait seconds by await counts; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Completed buffer depth and capacity
panels.description: Completed rollout groups waiting for training, against configured buffer capacity. Repeatedly empty buffers point to a generation shortfall; sustained full buffers point to slower consumption. Sampled zeros can miss short bursts; telemetry export enables these gauges.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Buffer dwell of trained groups
panels.description: Median, p95 and maximum time consumed groups waited between completion and trainer admission. A growing tail means useful work is sitting in the buffer and may become stale. Rejected groups are excluded; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Successful rollout-call latency
panels.description: Median, p95 and maximum wall time of successful rollout calls. A widening tail means a few calls are holding up generation; compare worker waits to distinguish serving from environment time. Failed calls are excluded; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Policy staleness at training
panels.description: Optimizer steps between generation and consumption of admitted groups. Zero means current-policy data; a rising tail approaches the configured staleness limit. Rejected groups are excluded, and a sync run shows zero only; telemetry export enables these observations.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Straggler proxy: rollout wait p99 ÷ p50
panels.description: Rollout-wait p99 divided by its median in each 30-minute bucket. A ratio near one means similar waits; a large ratio identifies unusually slow steps. This measures step-to-step spread across the run’s executions, and partial buckets use only observations inside the selected window. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

panels.title: Group dispositions / bucket
panels.description: Groups reaching each terminal disposition per display bucket. More consumed groups mean useful admission; rising rejected or stale-enqueue counts mean completed work is discarded. Groups count once at disposition, not at launch; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Tokens by group disposition / bucket
panels.description: Response tokens attached to each terminal group disposition per display bucket. Consumed tokens are useful work; rejected or stale tokens show the cost of discarded work. Compare with group counts to distinguish larger responses from more groups; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Rollouts completing during policy training
panels.description: Successful rollout calls finishing during each policy-training interval, separated by execution. More completed calls show generation overlapping the update; zero with complete coverage means no calls finished then. Clipped intervals or missing rollout records stay unknown rather than zero; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Inference sampled throughput by learner phase
panels.description: Sampled vLLM token throughput during each learner phase, separated by execution, collector, engine and counter. Compare generation during training and weight sync to locate interference. Counter resets and boundary-crossing intervals are excluded; missing sampled coverage is not zero throughput. Phase attribution requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: vLLM token throughput
panels.description: Prompt and generated-token throughput summed across inference engines. Rising prompt share can mean more prefill work; compare prefix-cache hit rate and the task’s sampling pattern before calling it inefficient. Rates use reset-aware per-engine counter deltas; requires engine telemetry. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

panels.title: vLLM queue and KV-cache usage
panels.description: Running/queued engine requests, with mean KV-cache occupancy on the right axis. A persistent queue with high occupancy and preemptions supports cache pressure; low occupancy can suggest scheduling or compute limits. Queue draining can be an intentional rollout boundary, and values are engine means; requires engine telemetry. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

panels.title: vLLM request latency (mean by stage)
panels.description: Mean queue, prefill, decode, first-token and end-to-end latency per finished request. Rising queue time means requests wait to start; rising decode time means generation slows. Means hide tails, and first-token/end-to-end stages overlap the other stages; requires engine telemetry. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

panels.title: vLLM KV-cache preemptions
panels.description: Engine requests evicted from KV cache and recomputed per bucket. Nonzero values identify work lost to cache pressure; compare occupancy and queue growth. Zero means no preemption was recorded, not that all cache costs disappeared. Engine preemption differs from pod or Iris preemption; requires engine telemetry. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

panels.title: Why vLLM requests finished
panels.description: Completed engine requests by finish reason per bucket. A growing length-limited share can explain changes in reward or response coverage. Finish reasons depend on the engine version and one rollout can create several requests; requires engine telemetry. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

panels.title: Prefix-cache hit rate
panels.description: Cached prompt tokens divided by queried prompt tokens across inference engines. A low rate with high prompt throughput suggests repeated prefill work. This is a token fraction, not a request-hit fraction, and sampling patterns affect it; requires engine telemetry. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No vLLM rows for this run. If the whole rank is blank, the engine exporter is down rather than six separate faults.

panels.title: What staleness is training using? (async; sync shows 0 only)
Staleness of trained groups: groups per step
panels.description: Admitted group counts by optimizer step and policy staleness. Growth in older buckets means more training work uses older weights; compare with reward and mismatch. Rejected groups are excluded and sync runs show zero only; telemetry export enables these observations.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Staleness of trained groups: tokens per step
panels.description: Consumed response tokens by optimizer step and policy staleness. Larger older buckets mean more of the batch’s tokens come from older policies. Token counts differ from group counts when response lengths differ; sync runs show zero only. Requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Trainer/vLLM logprob mismatch ρ (staleness 0)
panels.description: Trainer/vLLM probability mismatch on staleness-zero loss tokens. Large log-ratio tails or low ESS reveal a mismatch even without policy aging. Missing rollout logprobs leave gaps; sync runs have only the zero-staleness comparison. Requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Trainer/vLLM logprob mismatch by staleness bucket
panels.description: Mean absolute trainer/vLLM log-ratio across staleness buckets. A larger error in older buckets suggests aging policy data contributes to mismatch. Compare with the zero-staleness baseline; async-only buckets are absent for sync runs. Requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.description: Share of consumed loss tokens represented by complete uniform-staleness diagnostics. Higher coverage makes comparisons by staleness more representative; low coverage limits the conclusions. No observed tokens gives null, and sync runs have staleness zero only; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No valid token denominator

panels.title: Uniform-staleness diagnostic token coverage

panels.description: Response length, token-weighted log-ratio error, minimum ESS and mean reward for uniform-staleness batches. Compare rows at different staleness to see whether older data is less useful. Mixed-staleness or incomplete batches are excluded; sync runs can contribute staleness zero only. Requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No matching diagnostics.

panels.title: Uniform-staleness batch diagnostics
Where does Megatron policy-update time go?
Megatron policy wall across ranks
panels.description: Minimum, mean and maximum policy-update wall across observed rank-steps. A growing maximum above the mean suggests rank imbalance. Megatron phases are CPU wall time around asynchronous CUDA launches (clock_domain=cpu_dispatch_wall), so a phase can end before its GPU work does; requires trainer.policy_train_spans.

defaults.noValue: No learner phase observations. Check trainer.policy_train_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Learner memory by phase
panels.description: Largest observed allocated and reserved learner-memory peaks per phase, taking the maximum across selected ranks and executions. Peaks near device capacity leave little headroom; a widening reserved/allocated gap can indicate allocator pressure. Peaks need not occur simultaneously and values are GiB; requires trainer.policy_train_spans.

defaults.noValue: No learner phase observations. Check trainer.policy_train_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Megatron phase detail (newest 8 steps)
panels.description: Phase walls for each rank’s newest eight observed optimizer steps. Compare the same phase across ranks to find dispatch or synchronization outliers. At most 5,000 phase rows are shown. Megatron phases are CPU wall time around asynchronous CUDA launches (clock_domain=cpu_dispatch_wall), so a phase can end before its GPU work does; requires trainer.policy_train_spans.

defaults.noValue: No learner phase observations. Check trainer.policy_train_spans and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: What are this run’s GPUs doing? (run-wide)
SM and tensor-pipe activity on this run's nodes
panels.description: SM-active and tensor-active fractions on this run’s attributed nodes. High SM activity with low tensor activity suggests kernels doing little matrix work. Node-level attribution cannot isolate other workloads or ranks; requires node-agent DCGM reporting. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers. GPU detail is available for ranges of 7h or less; longer ranges show a zoom message.

defaults.noValue: No GPU data. Over 7h: zoom to 7h or less. Otherwise no node join: trainer rows carry no node_name, or the node agent is not reporting this cluster.

panels.title: GPU memory in use on this run's nodes
panels.description: Mean and peak framebuffer bytes across attributed GPUs. Peaks near capacity mean little device-memory headroom. The node-level values include every process on each card, not just learner allocations; requires node-agent DCGM reporting. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers. GPU detail is available for ranges of 7h or less; longer ranges show a zoom message.

defaults.noValue: No GPU data. Over 7h: zoom to 7h or less. Otherwise no node join: trainer rows carry no node_name, or the node agent is not reporting this cluster.

panels.title: NVLink against PCIe receive traffic
panels.description: NVLink and PCIe receive throughput summed across attributed GPUs. Compare changes with synchronization and step wall to identify transfer pressure. Receive counters describe links within the host, not end-to-end network throughput, and missing counters remain absent; requires node-agent DCGM reporting. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers. GPU detail is available for ranges of 7h or less; longer ranges show a zoom message.

defaults.noValue: No GPU data. Over 7h: zoom to 7h or less. Otherwise no node join: trainer rows carry no node_name, or the node agent is not reporting this cluster. Or no NVLink or PCIe counters from this cluster's node agent.

panels.title: PCIe replay errors and power on this run's GPUs
panels.description: GPUs with a positive PCIe replay-counter increase, alongside peak board power. Replays can identify link faults worth checking against host diagnostics. A counter reset contributes its new value, and absence from this table does not imply no GPU activity; requires node-agent DCGM reporting. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers. GPU detail is available for ranges of 7h or less; longer ranges show a zoom message.

defaults.noValue: No positive PCIe replay increase on this run's attributed GPUs in this window.

panels.title: Do trainer and vLLM logprobs agree?
Pre-update model log-ratio drift
panels.description: Trainer-minus-generation logprob drift before the policy update. Values near zero mean the trainer reproduces rollout probabilities; growing magnitude suggests policy drift or a serving/training mismatch. Only finite loss tokens contribute; requires rollout logprobs and trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Pre-update PPO-window pressure
panels.description: Fractions of finite loss tokens below and above the configured PPO ratio window before the update. Rising fractions mean more tokens encounter the clipping bounds; compare with staleness and logprob drift. This measures pressure against the configured bounds, not the applied correction; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Drift coverage and token-weight concentration
panels.description: Finite logprob coverage, missing rollout logprobs and importance-weight ESS fraction. High finite coverage and ESS are desirable; missing behavior data or concentrated weights weaken the comparison. ESS is a token-weight diagnostic, not a count of independent samples; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Mean squared model log-ratio
panels.description: Mean squared trainer-minus-vLLM logprob difference before the update. A rising value means larger probability mismatch, even when signed drift averages near zero. Only finite loss tokens contribute; requires rollout logprobs and trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Mean correction weight
panels.description: Mean off-policy correction weight over eligible tokens, including masked zeros. A falling mean means correction suppresses more of the batch’s effective contribution. Missing series mean correction is unconfigured or unobserved; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Correction activity
panels.description: Fractions of eligible tokens masked or truncated by correction, alongside policy-loss clipping. Rising fractions mean more proposed update weight is suppressed; compare with ESS and mismatch. Correction series are absent when correction is unconfigured; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Trainer logprob drift within the update
panels.description: Trainer logprob change within its own update, against probabilities recomputed at consumption. Growing tails or falling ESS show a larger update relative to that starting policy. This differs from rollout-time serving mismatch; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Position dependence of |log ρ|
panels.description: Absolute log-ratio drift near the first and last response tokens and in the middle. Larger errors late in responses can reveal position-dependent drift hidden by pooled averages. Serving mismatch and within-update drift have separate series and coverage; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: How much useful work do the configured resources produce?
Loss tokens trained per second
panels.description: Latest useful loss-token throughput using core and full-cycle denominators. Higher is better at comparable workloads; a wide gap shows work outside the core reducing overall throughput. Values describe the latest observed step in each series, not a window-wide average; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Useful tokens per configured role GPU-second
panels.description: Latest useful tokens per configured policy or inference GPU-second. Compare like workloads to spot declining resource efficiency. Configured GPU counts are denominators, not observed device usage or vLLM utilization; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Configured role GPU counts
panels.description: Configured policy and inference GPU counts for the latest observed step. Use them to interpret per-GPU rates and check placement assumptions. They describe requested topology, not healthy or busy devices; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Cumulative core GPU-hours in selected window
panels.description: Cumulative configured GPU-hours spent in complete core-step observations inside the selected window, per execution. Compare useful work against this cost at matched configurations. The total excludes startup, evaluation, checkpoints and export time and is not a billing meter; requires trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Is Ray spilling or filling its object store? (run-wide)
Ray object store occupancy
panels.description: Used share of the Ray object store across attributed nodes. Values approaching one indicate limited space and can precede spills or admission delays. The denominator is used plus free bytes, distinct from vLLM KV cache; requires Ray metric collection. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No Ray rows for this run. Non-Ray deployment, or the Ray metric bridge is off.

panels.title: Ray spill bytes
panels.description: Ray spill-manager bytes by state, averaged across attributed nodes. Pending spill or restore that does not drain suggests a stalled storage path. Pinned/pending values are occupancy; spilled/restored values are lifetime totals and are not additive states. Requires Ray metric collection. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No Ray rows for this run. Non-Ray deployment, or the Ray metric bridge is off.

panels.title: Which diagnostics explain missing or stalled work?
Services reporting this run
panels.description: Services, roles and metric sources reporting this run, with their latest observation times. Missing expected services or old records can explain blank panels; the expected set depends on the workload and whether engines report independently or through the trainer. The node agent has no run id and is absent here. Run-wide: this panel ignores the Job and Execution pickers.

defaults.noValue: No services under this run_id in this window.

panels.title: Process lifecycle and terminal export counts
panels.description: Latest lifecycle or terminal event per process, with lost and queued record counts from its terminal event. A missing terminal event leaves the counts empty.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Span coverage: clock domain and failed steps
panels.description: Observed steps and failed steps by role and timing clock domain. Missing coverage identifies which timing panels cannot describe the selected attempts; failures distinguish interrupted from completed work. Missing outcomes remain unknown rather than zero.

defaults.noValue: No spans. The run reported a policy_step, so the trainer's timing sink is not reaching Finelog.

panels.title: Exporter and nonfinite observations
panels.description: Lost/rejected export records and nonfinite training values by process. Increasing export counts mean observations are missing; nonfinite values can signal an invalid update. Nonfinite values sum deltas, while exporter counters use their maximum cumulative reading; nonfinite observations require trainer.training_metrics.

defaults.noValue: No training-metric observations. Check trainer.training_metrics and the selected Job/Execution.

panels.title: Signed timing residuals
panels.description: Signed rollout-call and Megatron residual walls after named child phases. Large positive residuals identify unassigned time; negative values indicate overlapping observations and remain visible. Rollout residuals require trainer.rollout_spans; Megatron residuals require trainer.policy_train_spans. Megatron phases are CPU wall time around asynchronous CUDA launches (clock_domain=cpu_dispatch_wall), so a phase can end before its GPU work does.

defaults.noValue: No matching attempt observations. Check the window, Job/Execution and Services reporting.

panels.title: Driver event-loop lag
panels.description: Worst observed delay of the driver event loop in each bucket. Sustained lag can delay admission, telemetry and control work even when device work continues. The monitor samples once per second; requires trainer.rollout_spans.

defaults.noValue: No rollout-span observations. Check trainer.rollout_spans and the selected Job/Execution.
